lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.13 - A Listen and say. Then practise.

details: Listen and say introduces students to new comparatives and allows them to practise comparing objects using the target language.
Look for careful listening, correct pronunciation and use of comparatives, particularly with adjectives ending in -y.
“I’m so excited! We’re going to the beach today. I’m going to bring my pretty swimsuit, my clean towel and my big life ring. What’s that? Your life ring is bigger than mine?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.13 - B. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer gives students controlled practice using the target language to ask and respond to simple questions using comparatives.
Look for accurate use of comparatives in questions and responses.

“Let’s imagine we’re on this beach now. Lying back and enjoying the sun. It’s so nice… I think I’m going to sleep! Can you practice comparing things? Ask and answer as many as you can.  I’ll ask you when I wake up!”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.71 - A Look and write

details: Look and write asks students to identify and spell the adjective and comparative that matches each picture, reinforcing whole-word memory.
Look for correct spelling of both adjectives and comparatives.
“What a lovely day we’ve had. Can you help me find my things to pack in my bag? I had a pretty dress,  a big cup and a clean t-shirt. Help me work out which ones are mine!”

Look for comprehension of each statement and confidence selecting the correct answers.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book P.14, 52 - Speaking Find the Differences

details: The Find the Differences activity allows students to practice using the target language in pairs, taking it in turns to find a difference between the two pictures.
Look for turn taking and correct and confident use of comparatives to compare the pictures.
“We all went to the same beach, right? But these pictures aren’t quite the same? Can you work in pairs to find all the differences? Tell me how many you find altogether!”
